title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1976 IHÉS lecture notes on the divided-power de Rham complex. Here c_{a,b} denotes the binomial coefficient (a+b)!/(a! b!), the structure constant for multiplying divided powers: x^{[a]} x^{[b]} = c_{a,b} x^{[a+b]}. Some sequence (ξ_k)_{k≥N}, presumably coefficients of a cocycle or of a module element in a divided-power algebra over Z_p, satisfies relation (1): c_{l,k} ξ_k = c_{l,k-i} ξ_{k+l} for all l ≥ 0. The goal is to show ξ_k = 0 for all k ≥ N.

The page has three parts.

(1) End of the proof of Lemma 1.1. Take h = i+j and h' = i+j', with c_{i,j} and c_{i,j'} units in Z_p. Apply relation (1) with l = h'-h = j'-j to get c_{j'-j, j+i} ξ_h = c_{j'-j, j} ξ_{h'}. On the previous page Grothendieck showed the two coefficients have equal p-adic valuation. So when condition (5) holds, both are units and ξ_h = 0 ⇔ ξ_{h'} = 0.

(2) Proof of Lemma 1: if one ξ_k with k ≥ N and c_{i,k-i} a unit vanishes, then all such ξ_k vanish. Write i and j = k-i in base p with r+1 digits. By Lucas/Kummer, c_{i,j} ≢ 0 (mod p) iff i_α + j_α ≤ p-1 for every α, i.e. there are no carries. Set δ_α = p-1-(i_α+j_α) and j'_α = j_α + δ_α = p-1-i_α. Put j' = Σ j'_α p^α and δ = j'-j = Σ δ_α p^α. Then:
- c_{i,j'} is a unit, since i_α + j'_α = p-1 (no carry);
- c_{δ,j} is a unit, since δ_α + j_α = j'_α ≤ p-1.
So Lemma 1.1 applies, and ξ_k = 0 ⇔ ξ_{i+j'} = 0, where i+j' = p^{r+1}-1. Every admissible k is thereby linked to the single index p^{r+1}-1 (r large); the next page completes this comparison.

(3) A marginal 'simpler presentation': choose r with p^r > i+j and δ = p^r-1-(i+j). Since p^r-1 has all base-p digits equal to p-1, every binomial among i, j, δ is a p-adic unit, giving the same conclusion with h' = p^r-1.

This is an elementary combinatorial lemma on p-adic valuations of binomial coefficients, presumably serving a computation of the cohomology of (or a vanishing statement in) the divided-power polynomial/de Rham complex over Z_p.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Lemma 1.1 implicitly requires h' ≥ h ≥ N; this holds because j' ≥ j.
In the margin, the unit condition written c_{(i+j),δ} is not literally the c_{δ,j} needed in Lemma 1.1. It does imply it, since there are no carries anywhere when i+j+δ = p^r-1, so this is harmless.

ideas.what: Nonvanishing mod p of binomial coefficients characterized digitwise by the absence of carries in base p
ideas.where_published: Standard; used implicitly in Berthelot's crystalline cohomology work

ideas.what: Completing base-p digits to p-1 to connect any no-carry pair (i,j) to the index p^{r+1}-1 through unit-coefficient relations, propagating vanishing of the ξ_k
ideas.modern_name: Elementary p-adic combinatorics of divided-power structure constants

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, correct combinatorial lemma on p-adic units among binomial coefficients (Lucas/Kummer), used as a step in a divided-power computation; nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Margin: 'soit r tel que p^r > i+j' is consistent with the image and the mathematics (δ = p^r-1-(i+j) ≥ 0).
'j' ≥ j (dans ℕ)': the image reads '(dans N)', i.e. as natural numbers.
